headline: RBI mandates 20% Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve on large INR forex derivative contracts
effective_from: Applies to foreign exchange derivative contracts undertaken after issuance of the Directions (October 10, 2026)
summary_points: Authorised Dealers must maintain a Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR) for INR forex derivative contracts with users.
Applies to contracts above USD 2 million equivalent hedging current account transactions where the user buys foreign currency against INR.
Splitting transactions across one or more Authorised Dealers to avoid the threshold is a violation of the Directions.

rows: Forex derivative contracts involving INR with users
Notional value above USD 2 million equivalent
Hedging current account transactions; user purchasing foreign currency against INR
20% of INR equivalent of notional amount of each contract
Cash in India with RBI, deposited daily
Multiple transactions to circumvent threshold treated as violation

who_is_affected: Authorised Dealer banks and corporate users who hedge current account exposures by buying foreign currency against INR through derivatives above USD 2 million.
action_required: Authorised Dealers should set up daily cash FERR maintenance and CIMS reporting, and users should reassess hedging costs and avoid splitting contracts to bypass the threshold.

social.linkedin:
RBI has introduced a Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR) for Authorised Dealers, through A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 26 dated October 10, 2026.

Key points:

• The reserve applies to forex derivative contracts involving INR with users, where the notional value exceeds USD 2 million equivalent and the contract hedges current account transactions with the user purchasing foreign currency against INR.

• The reserve is 20% of the INR equivalent of the notional amount of each contract, deposited in cash with RBI daily and maintained until the contract terminates.

• Attempts to bypass the threshold through multiple transactions with one or more Authorised Dealers will be treated as a violation.

• Authorised Dealers must report FERR details daily through CIMS.

The Directions apply to contracts undertaken after issuance and are issued under FEMA Sections 10(4) and 11(1) and Section 45W of the RBI Act.

Treasury teams and corporates with import-related hedging should assess the cost impact.

Please verify with the official RBI circular before acting.
